title: Launch security gate: RBAC v2, audit schema, evidence automation & SIEM export checklist
content:
Purpose:
This checklist is the canonical pre-launch security gate for releases that change inference-side security controls (RBAC v2), logging and SIEM exports, or that require temporary exceptions. It combines checklist items for RBAC validation, audit log schema verification, automated evidence collection, SIEM export mapping, and the exception/approval template used by Security.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted API features, Dedicated deployments that affect role mappings, and Private control-plane changes that impact audit or SIEM pipelines.
- Not intended for purely UI copy fixes; use discretion.

Quick summary of RBAC v2 expectations (pre-flight):
- Role model must be finalized in the deployment branch: roles, inheritance, and allowed actions are explicit. Typical roles we expect to see: runtime_monitor (read metrics, read logs), model_ops (deploy models, rollout management), rw_admin (full runtime admin), billing_viewer (billing dashboards only), svc_token (service account with scoped permissions).
- Principle of least privilege: confirm no role includes wildcards for model:write unless justified.
- Service accounts: each automated system must have its own svc_token and an expiration or rotation policy. Confirm service account ID is present in the change set.
- SSO / SCIM sync: for any human role assignments, verify mapping to SSO groups and that SCIM provisioning will not break during rollout.
- RBAC migration plan: if the change includes changes to role names/IDs, include a migration and rollback plan and a db-migration ticket.

Checklist: RBAC v2 validation (owner: eng-security / product-ops)
- [ ] Role manifest file included in PR and matches RFC: roles.yaml present and schema validated.
- [ ] Automated unit tests for role-to-permission matrix included and passing.
- [ ] Integration test: deploy to staging with sample principals and ensure enforcement (deny path exercised). Link: INFRA-2197.
- [ ] No direct principal->admin grants without documented business justification.
- [ ] Migration script included if role ids change. Backout script prepared.

Audit log schema verification (owner: observability / security-engineering)
- Expected core audit fields (minimum):
  - timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
  - event_id (uuid)
  - actor (string; e.g., user/email or service)
  - actor_id (opaque id)
  - principal_type (human | service | machine)
  - resource_type (deployment | model | route | key | config)
  - resource_id (string)
  - action (string; e.g., model.deploy, api.call, key.rotate)
  - outcome (success | failure | denied)
  - request_id (for correlating traces)
  - trace_id (if available from tracing system)
  - tokens_requested (int)
  - tokens_returned (int)
  - response_latency_ms (int)
  - model_name (string)
  - model_revision (string)
  - node_id (string)
  - region (string)
  - environment (prod|staging|dev)
  - api_key_hash (hashed, do not log raw key)

- [ ] Confirm schema version is bumped for this release and documented as audit.schema=v2.x in release notes.
- [ ] Ensure PII is not captured; if PII must be logged (rare), it must be masked and approved by legal.
- [ ] Validate sample logs (>=10 events across success/failure/deny paths) are produced by the staging run and attached to the release ticket.

SIEM export and parser mapping (owner: observability / sec-ops)
- Required exports: all audit logs must be forwarded to SecOps SIEM (ELK cluster and Splunk ingestion points) with guaranteed delivery (at-least-once).
- Recommended mapping to SIEM fields (suggested ECS aligned names):
  - ecs.@timestamp <- timestamp
  - event.id <- event_id
  - user.name <- actor
  - user.id <- actor_id
  - user.type <- principal_type
  - event.action <- action
  - event.outcome <- outcome
  - trace.id <- trace_id
  - http.request_id <- request_id (if HTTP path)
  - cloud.region <- region
  - host.name <- node_id
  - service.name <- service (e.g., inference-runtime)
  - process.name <- process/component producing the event
  - redwood.model.name <- model_name (custom namespace)
  - redwood.model.revision <- model_revision

- [ ] Confirm log forwarder config committed (file path: ops/log-forwarders/inference-forwarder-*.yaml).
- [ ] Verify parser compatibility: add grok/ingest pipeline patterns. Example Elastic ingest pipeline entry included in linked GitHub PR.
- [ ] SIEM retention & index settings: ensure audit indexes respect 365d retention for compliance; shorter indexes for debug logs ok.
- [ ] Detection owners informed: list of SIEM detection rules that might need tuning due to new events (credential usage anomalies, mass-deploy events).

Evidence automation (owner: release-engineering / sec-automation)
- Goal: automatically gather the minimal artifact set required for sign-off and for any post-launch audits.
- Required artifacts to attach to release ticket (automated if possible):
  - RBAC role manifest (roles.yaml)
  - Migration plan and backout instructions (markdown)
  - Sample audit logs from staging run (>=10 events) in ndjson
  - SIEM ingest test report (ingest success counts, index names)
  - Test matrix results for access-deny/allow paths
  - Evidence of key rotation policy for any new service accounts

- Automation pointers:
  - evidence_gather script: scripts/evidence_gather.sh --release ${RELEASE_TAG} --out artifacts/${RELEASE_TAG}.tgz
  - It should fetch: roles.yaml, migrations/*.sql, staging-logs/*.ndjson, siem/ingest-test.json, test-results/access-matrix.csv
  - Upload target: artifacts attached to JIRA ticket SEC-482 or the release checklist in the release tooling.
- [ ] Run CI job: release/evidence-collector and attach generated tgz to the release task.
- [ ] Manual checklist item to confirm artifacts are complete if automation failed.

Exception approval (temporary deviations) (owner: security-reviewer)
- Exceptions are allowed only with a documented compensating control and an expiry date. Exceptions must be tracked as a JIRA ticket with component=security-exception.
- Minimum exception template:
  - title: short description
  - justification: business need and why change cannot be implemented in time
  - scope: who/what is impacted (principals, services)
  - compensating controls: e.g., extra logging, IP allowlist, time-limited creds, manual approvals
  - risk assessment: low|medium|high and rationale
  - owner and approvers: security lead, product manager, SRE lead, legal if PII
  - expiry: YYYY-MM-DD (maximum 90 days unless escalated)

- Approval flow (typical):
  - 1) Submit JIRA ticket with template, link to release PR and artifacts (SEC-482)
  - 2) Security engineer (level 2) reviews and requests clarifications
  - 3) Security manager signs off (comment + resolution) or escalates to CISO for high risk
  - 4) SRE or infra lead provides mitigation ops playbook
  - 5) Product PM acknowledges residual risk and confirms rollback plan

- [ ] If an exception is approved, add a post-launch verification task that circles back before expiry.

Launch sign-off block (to be completed before merge to main):
- Engineering lead (runtime): ____________________  name: Samir Rao  date: 2026-01-10  comment: "RBAC tests green, migration included"
- Security reviewer: ____________________  name: Ayesha Kapoor  date: 2026-01-10  comment: "Audit schema validated; SIEM ingest verified"
- Observability owner: ____________________  name: Elena Grayson  date: 2026-01-10  comment: "Ingest pipeline updated; detection teams notified"
- Product owner sign-off: ____________________  name: Priya Patel  date: 2026-01-10  comment: "Business ready; rollback plan approved"

Post-launch monitoring & verification (72h window):
- [ ] Confirm no unexpected permission-denied alerts correlated with rollout (SecOps).
- [ ] Monitor SIEM error rates and ingestion drops for 48h (Observability).
- [ ] Run smoke replay to exercise deny/allow matrix in production (SRE).
- [ ] Evidence package persisted to archive (compliance) and attached to release record.

Known risks & mitigation notes (notes-to-self style):
- If RBAC migration touches model ownership records, be careful of transient authorization errors during rolling deploy. Consider short-circuiting runtime cache invalidation.
- SIEM ingest pipeline must tolerate at-least-once duplicates; downstream detections should dedupe on event.id.
- Evidence automation sometimes fails for very large logs; cap sample to first 5000 events and document sampling strategy.

Open questions (to resolve before final sign-off):
- Do we need to add model input fingerprinting to logs for model output alignment audits? (Security + Legal)
- Should audit logs include a lightly hashed prompt_id for debugging without exposing content? (privacy review pending)

Attachments checklist (for release ticket):
- roles.yaml (committed)
- migrations/*.sql or migrations/*.py (if present)
- artifacts/${RELEASE_TAG}.tgz from evidence_gather
- staging-logs/sample.ndjson (>=10 events)
- SIEM ingest test report JSON

References and quick links:
- RBAC v2 design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/RBAC+v2+Design
- Audit schema tracker: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/Audit+Schema+Roadmap
- SIEM onboarding runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/SIEM+Ingest+Runbook
- JIRA: SEC-482 (current exception request)

If anything on this checklist fails, mark the release as "hold" and escalate to Security Pager.

Notes to self (informal):
- Remember to attach the ingest pipeline snippet from github PR 412; the grok pattern had an edge case for empty model_revision.
- Double-check that api_key_hash field uses HKDF salt derived per-tenant (not global) — Miguel to confirm.

End of doc.
